title: Seacliff Systems implementation kickoff and connectivity huddle
summary: Kickoff to align on network connectivity, security posture, rollout milestones for a pilot of Redwood Private in Seacliff's VPC. SE-led portion covered autoscaling expectations, model pinning, and KV cache behavior. Customer raised questions about key management, audit logs, and latency SLOs. Agreed next steps include exchange of diagrams, access for smoke tests, and a pilot timeline.
action_items: Marcus Wu - Share VPC CIDR blocks, peering contact, and firewall policy by 2026-07-05
Jordan Lee - Send onboarding playbook, pilot checklist, and access spreadsheet by 2026-07-03
Priya Nambiar - Prepare a lightweight bench script and perf acceptance criteria by 2026-07-07
Samir Patel - Provide KMS key rotation policy and compliance contacts by 2026-07-06
Ethan Cole - Schedule follow-up enablement session with ops team (30-45 min) by 2026-07-08
next_steps: Exchange network diagram and create temporary peering link for smoke tests
Set up Redwood Private trial tenant with 2 reserved slots for pilot
Run small synthetic perf run and share results (SE to lead)
Customer to confirm pilot owners and success metrics (latency < 120ms p50 for 128-token prompts)
Agree on date for first bench test: 2026-07-10
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 47m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nambiar (Redwood SE), Ethan Cole (Redwood CSM); Lena Ortiz (CTO, Seacliff), Marcus Wu (SRE Lead), Amina Durrani (Platform Eng), Samir Patel (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh, super excited to kick this off. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Lena: Hey, Lena here.
[00:07] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:09] Amina: Amina on the line.
[00:11] Samir: Samir here.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. We're shooting for two main outcomes today: align on networking and security for Redwood Private in your VPC, and land the pilot scope and timeline. Quick note, audio may be a little rough on my end, sorry if I cut out.
[00:25] Priya: I'll take point on the SE stuff in the middle part—network requirements, perf expectations, that sort of thing.
[00:33] Ethan: And I'll cover onboarding cadence and ops handoffs at the end.

[00:40] Lena: Sounds good. For context, our objective is to run a pilot that replaces some of our current in-house model serving for customer-facing chat in one region. Security and latency are non-negotiable.
[00:53] Jordan: Totally. Marcus, can you walk us through your networking shape briefly?
[00:57] Marcus: Yeah, so we run in AWS in us-east-1, multi-account. We'll likely want a VPC peering or transit gateway. CIDRs are 10.10.0.0/16 for infra and 10.20.0.0/16 for services, roughly. We have strict egress rules, usually we allow only a few destinations.
[01:15] Jordan: Cool—would you be open to opening a temporary peering with a restricted set of endpoints for the smoke tests?
[01:22] Marcus: Yeah, temporary peering is fine, need the exact IPs and ports.
[01:26] Priya: For our smoke tests we typically need outbound to the control plane on TCP 443 and inbound for health checks on a small range—I'll paste our typical ports in the follow-up doc. Also, K V cache behavior: if you have long-running sessions we can keep warm caches but need to know session patterns.
[01:44] Amina: Sorry, K V cache—do you mean key value cache, like the KV cache for transformer logits? We've got sticky sessions via our gateway.
[01:51] Priya: Yeah, KV cache as in the tokens/kv store, sorry, bad wording, sometimes the transcript—um—the point is caching will affect latency and cost. If sessions stick to a host we can exploit local cache.

[02:05] Samir: On security, two big asks: KMS integration for key ownership and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also we require SSO: SAML S S O over OIDC, enterprise SSO.
[02:15] Jordan: That's fine. We support KMS integrations; for Private we can either federate to your KMS or use a customer-managed key in your tenant. Audit logs: we can stream event logs to your syslog/S3, and we have per-request tracing tokens.
[02:31] Marcus: What's the retention on those logs by default?
[02:34] Ethan: Default retention is 30 days in the console, but for enterprise we can arrange longer retention as an add-on. We'll capture request-level metadata but redact full prompt text unless you opt-in.
[02:47] Marcus: Good. We need the prompts to be off by default for compliance.

[02:52] Priya: Ok quick SE deep dive—our recommended pilot is 2 reserved slots, one model pinned (we can pin a 7B open model or a quantized 13B depending on your latency targets) and a small canary route. For 128 token prompts we're seeing p50 around 80-110ms on modern instances with batching disabled; with batching on p95 can creep up. Your target?
[03:18] Lena: We want p50 under 120ms and p95 under 400ms for interactive chat in region.
[03:24] Priya: That's doable. If you want guaranteed p50 <120, we recommend dedicated capacity (which is what Redwood Private gives you). We'll size based on concurrency; what concurrency are you expecting?
[03:35] Amina: Initial will be very small, maybe 10 concurrent in the pilot, but plan to ramp to 200 per region after quarter two.
[03:44] Priya: Ok, for 10 concurrent pinned on a 7B quantized model that's easily met. For 200 you'll want autoscale rules + burst pools or a larger model with different kernels.

[03:56] Jordan: Quick commercial note, pilot pricing is usually credit-based, we'll provide a pilot quote.
[04:00] Marcus: Uh quick question: do you support on-prem at all? We've got some sensitive workloads we might want to keep air-gapped later.
[04:07] Jordan: Yes we do Redwood Private has an on-prem option though it's more involved; we'll scope that if pilot is successful.

[04:15] Amina: On integrations—how does deployment look? Do we push our models or do you host them?
[04:20] Priya: For Private we can host the model within your tenant; model artifacts can live in your S3 and we can reference them, or we can pull curated open models into the private runtime depending on licensing. You retain model version control and can pin versions.
[04:35] Samir: What about encryption at rest—are model weights encrypted with our KMS?
[04:39] Jordan: Yes we support encrypting artifacts with customer-managed KMS keys. We'll need IAM role assumption details.

[04:47] [05:00] Marcus: Another operational question: how will we do rollbacks if a model regresses?
[05:05] Priya: Rollouts are via the Console or API—canary, A/B or immediate. You can pin older model versions and route a percent to fallback. We also integrate with your CI for automated rollbacks on evaluation failures.

[05:22] Lena: For success criteria for the pilot, we're proposing: 1) p50 < 120ms for targeted routes, 2) no PII in logs by default, 3) ability to rotate KMS keys without downtime, 4) clear audit delivery into our SIEM.
[05:40] Jordan: Sounds good. Ethan, anything on enablement?
[05:43] Ethan: We'll do a 2-week enablement window: week 1 network and baseline smoke tests; week 2 perf runs and runbook handover. I'll own scheduling and runbook docs. We'll also provide a runbook template.

[06:00] [06:30] Marcus: What metrics do you surface in the console? Token-level cost?
[06:35] Priya: Yes token-level cost, latency buckets, per-route error rate, and trace IDs so you can correlate logs. Our tracing hooks capture per-request metadata.

[06:45] Samir: On compliance, do you have SOC 2 Type II reports?
[06:48] Jordan: Yes we do, I can share a redacted pack; for Private deployments we also provide architecture diagrams and compliance attestations.
[06:57] Samir: Great. Send those.

[07:02] Lena: About timeline—we've got a regulatory review window mid-July. We'd like pilot smoke tests before July 15 so the results can feed into the review. Is that possible?
[07:12] Jordan: Yes, we can aim for bench tests week of July 10. Priya, can you commit to having scripts ready by 7/7?
[07:20] Priya: Yep I'll have a bench script and perf criteria ready by then.

[07:26] [07:50] Amina: Regarding secrets, do you support HSM-backed KMS or only cloud KMS?
[07:55] Jordan: We can integrate with cloud KMS and customers who require FIPS or HSM-backed keys can bring an HSM via our KMS connectors; we'll need to map that out with Samir.

[08:08] Samir: We'll send over our key rotation policy.

[08:12] [08:30] Jordan: Ok let's recap real quick—Marcus to share network CIDRs and firewall owner; Samir to share KMS policy; Jordan to send onboarding pack; Priya to prepare bench script; Ethan to schedule follow-up. Does that capture it?
[08:45] Lena: Yes. Also we want to ensure prompts aren't stored; default must be redacted.
[08:52] Priya: We'll set prompt redaction off by default and show you the config.

[09:00] [09:30] Marcus: Small thing—do you have any recommended IAM role names or trust principals for the workload?
[09:36] Priya: We'll add our recommended role and least-privilege policy to the onboarding doc.

[09:43] Jordan: Any blockers on your side today?
[09:46] Lena: Not blockers, just internal approval chain for network changes. We'll need to loop in cloud infra owners after this.
[09:54] Jordan: Ok we'll include a short deck for the infra reviewers.

[10:02] [10:30] Amina: Can we get a quick sketch or diagram of the control plane interactions? I want to be sure of egress patterns.
[10:36] Priya: Yup I'll include a sequence diagram and a minimal ports/IPs list.

[10:42] [11:00] Ethan: I'll propose two meeting times for the infra deep-dive next week: Tue or Thu 30-min.
[11:06] Marcus: Tue morning works for me.

[11:10] Jordan: Alright if there's nothing else we'll call it. Thanks all.

[11:18] [crosstalk]

[11:45] 
End of transcript.

Notes on transcript quality: Some acronyms were jumbled (SAML S S O, K V cache spelled out), and a few proper nouns may be mis-transcribed. There were short gaps and brief crosstalk in the last 5 minutes.
